How is SCRIPE-Backend architected for zero-trust, multi-DB modular scale?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE-Backend runs a zero-trust .NET 10 modular monolith powered by AstraFlow 2.3.0 that can split into server roles and multi-DB engines without code changes.1

  1. Every request passes ordered origin, JWT revocation, CSRF, replay, and tenant guards before reaching a controller.2
  2. AstraFlow runs six ordered behaviors (Logging to Caching + Idempotency) and sequential notifications across 927+ handlers.3
  3. Startup DI guards enforce cross-module contract pairs so server-role splits fail at boot, not on traffic.4
  4. BaseDbContext commits domain rows, outbox_messages, and idempotency_receipts per module schema across PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle.5

Applies to.NET 10AstraFlow 2.3.018 Modules927+ CQRS HandlersPostgreSQL / SQL Server / Oracle

1

How do requests flow from edge ingress to schema-isolated persistence?

Diagram structure
  • Clients & Edge client
  • JWT & Revocation identity_auth
  • Middleware Pipeline http_pipeline
  • OTel & Real-Time observability
  • API Controllers controllers
  • Redis L1 & Locks redis_cache
  • AstraFlow Mediator mediator
  • EventBus & Inbox event_bus
  • 18 Domain Modules handlers
  • CatalogPricing Engine pricing_engine
  • BaseDbContext base_dbcontext
  • OutboxProcessorJob outbox_processor
  • Schema-Isolated DBs module_db
  • client → http_pipeline · HTTPS
  • http_pipeline → identity_auth · verify JWT
  • http_pipeline → observability · traces & hubs
  • http_pipeline → controllers · PBAC route
  • controllers → mediator · ISender.Send
  • mediator → redis_cache · L1 cache & lock
  • mediator → handlers · dispatch
  • handlers → pricing_engine · Quote Contract
  • handlers → base_dbcontext · SaveChanges
  • pricing_engine → base_dbcontext · Freeze Quote
  • base_dbcontext → module_db · atomic commit
  • module_db → outbox_processor · poll outbox
  • outbox_processor → event_bus · publish batch
  • event_bus → mediator · INotification
  1. Middleware Pipeline ↗

    Enforces Cloudflare origin secret, rate limits, JWT revocation via IAccountRevocationCache, CSRF, replay nonce, and X-Tenant-Context.

  2. API Controllers ↗

    Versioned REST controllers check [PermissionRequired] and send typed commands to ISender without business exceptions.

  3. AstraFlow Mediator ↗

    Runs Logging, Validation, Idempotency, Authorization, Caching, and PerformanceBehavior.

  4. 18 Module Handlers ↗

    Executes domain logic and synchronous cross-module reads (ICatalogPricingCalculationService) returning Result<T>.

  5. BaseDbContext & UoW ↗

    Applies expression-tree TenantId filters, UTC conversion, RowVersion bumps, and atomic outbox capture in one transaction.

  6. OutboxProcessorJob ↗

    Acquires distributed lock and publishes pending events to IEventBus or IDomainEventPublisher.

2

How does a mutating command guarantee at-most-once execution and at-least-once events?

Diagram structure
  • API Controller ctrl
  • IdempotencyBehavior med
  • Redis L1 Cache cache
  • CommandHandler hdl
  • BaseDbContext (DB) db
  • OutboxProcessorJob outbox
  • ctrl → med · Send(Command + IdempotencyKey)
  • med → cache · GET idempotency:receipt
  • cache → med · L1 Miss
  • med → db · TX 1: INSERT InProgress claim (2m lease)
  • db → med · Claim committed
  • med → hdl · next() -> Handle(Command)
  • hdl → db · TX 2: SaveChanges (Entity + OutboxMessage)
  • med → db · TX 2/3: UPDATE Receipt Status=Completed (AES-GCM)
  • med → cache · SET L1 receipt cache (24h TTL)
  • med → ctrl · Result<T> (201 Created)
  • outbox → db · Poll unprocessed OutboxMessages (Batch=50)
  • db → outbox · Pending Domain / Integration Events
  • outbox → db · Mark ProcessedOn = UtcNow

Why three separate persistence phases?

Transaction 1 commits the InProgress claim row immediately so concurrent duplicate requests hit the unique index (TenantId, ActorKey, Operation, KeyHash) and return 409 Conflict instead of racing inside the handler.6
